system.boundary: Build a closed-loop Simulink navigation model for a car-like mobile robot on a known two-dimensional binary occupancy map.
engineering_objects: The model must generate a collision-free global route, repeatedly produce a locally feasible trajectory from the current robot state, execute bounded linear and angular commands through a bicycle-kinematic plant, and feed the simulated pose back into local planning.
it does not require SLAM, raw sensor processing, moving-obstacle prediction, or high-fidelity wheel and terrain dynamics.

modes_and_events: Build a closed-loop Simulink navigation model for a car-like mobile robot on a known two-dimensional binary occupancy map.

The model must generate a collision-free global route, repeatedly produce a locally feasible trajectory from the current robot state, execute bounded linear and angular commands through a bicycle-kinematic plant, and feed the simulated pose back into local planning.
If a local solution becomes infeasible, the model must retain a useful feasible prefix, correct the command, or request a new global route instead of bypassing the constraint.

interfaces.name: MapMatrix
interfaces.description: MATLAB base-workspace input declared by the current public task contract.
interfaces.range_or_shape: Read MapMatrix, StartPose, GoalPose, ObstacleSafetyMargin, MinimumTurningRadius, MaxLinearVelocity, and MaxAngularVelocity from the MATLAB base workspace. MapMatrix is a known binary occupancy matrix with zero meaning free and one meaning occupied (unitless); StartPose and GoalPose are 1-by-3 real vectors ordered [x_m, y_m, heading_rad]; ObstacleSafetyMargin is a real scalar in [0.8, 1.3] m; MinimumTurningRadius is a real scalar in [2.0, 2.5] m; MaxLinearVelocity is a real scalar in [10, 16] m/s; and MaxAngularVelocity is a real scalar in [0.75, 0.9] rad/s.
